lesson: When revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy implies a positive tailwind and credit_spread_baa and yield_curve_10y_2y show no stress, do not let a negative revenue_growth_yoy alone set the bucket; anchor the central estimate to the macro-adjusted growth and treat revenue_growth_mean_5y as a secondary drag, not the default.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits below revenue_growth_mean_5y by more than one revenue_growth_std_5y, treat mean reversion toward the 5-year mean as the default and let it set the modal bucket, rather than letting the trailing yoy value alone pick base. Use revenue_macro_beta only to widen the distribution, not to shift its center, unless yield_curve_10y_2y is negative or credit_spread_baa is rising.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is non-negative and credit_spread_baa is low or not widening, do not let a negative revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy override revenue_growth_mean_5y as the anchor; check unemployment_rate and credit_spread_baa explicitly before assigning a bear probability above 0.5.

When revenue_growth_yoy is above the 10% bull threshold and revenue_growth_std_5y is high, do not let revenue_growth_mean_5y set the central bucket. Treat the recent yoy reading as the central case and keep mean reversion as a tail weight, since a wide std weakens the 5y mean as an anchor.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits above revenue_growth_mean_5y and yield_curve_10y_2y is positive with gdp_growth_yoy positive, do not place the bucket below base on mean reversion alone; treat the 5y mean as a weak anchor and call bear only when a confirming macro signal such as yield_curve_10y_2y < 0 or a rising credit_spread_baa is present.

When revenue_growth_yoy exceeds revenue_growth_mean_5y by more than one revenue_growth_std_5y, do not default to mean reversion toward the base range. Treat the recent growth as possible persistence and keep bull at least as likely as base unless credit_spread_baa is rising or yield_curve_10y_2y is below zero.

When revenue_growth_yoy exceeds revenue_growth_mean_5y by more than one revenue_growth_std_5y, and revenue_macro_beta is above 1 with gdp_growth_yoy positive, weight persistence of recent growth above mean reversion and rank the bull bucket first instead of defaulting to the 0-10% base. Mean reversion is the default only when the recent deviation sits within one std of the 5y mean.

When revenue_growth_yoy is above revenue_growth_mean_5y and positive, do not rank the bear bucket first on mean reversion alone; treat the revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy headwind as unconfirmed unless yield_curve_10y_2y is below 0 or credit_spread_baa is rising, and otherwise keep base as the leading bucket.

When revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy implies a large negative macro effect, do not discard it because of unit concerns. Let it pull the call toward base or bear, and shrink revenue_growth_yoy toward revenue_growth_mean_5y when the two diverge sharply.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one revenue_growth_std_5y above revenue_growth_mean_5y, and revenue_macro_beta is high while the macro snapshot is benign (gdp_growth_yoy near trend, yield_curve_10y_2y positive), weight the recent momentum over the mean-reversion default and shift probability toward the bucket that momentum implies. Treat a high revenue_macro_beta as a signal that benign macro can push upside as well as downside.

When (revenue_growth_yoy - revenue_growth_mean_5y) / revenue_growth_std_5y is below 1 and gdp_growth_yoy is positive, weight persistence of revenue_growth_yoy over mean reversion. Check the z-score arithmetic before using it, because the analyst's stated 2.8 std gap was really about 0.9 std.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero (say below 0.01) or credit_spread_baa has no trend reading, treat that as an unresolved growth warning rather than as no warning, and subtract the macro drag (revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy) from the central estimate before assigning bull probability. Cap the bull probability unless growth still clears 10% after that drag and the revenue_growth_std_5y band.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits above revenue_growth_mean_5y but the mean is within one revenue_growth_std_5y of the bucket threshold, do not treat the yoy strength as bull support; anchor on the 5y distribution, which reverts toward the mean and leaves base as a likely outcome, and cut the bull probability accordingly.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero (say below 0.01) and revenue_macro_beta is strongly negative (below -0.5), treat the curve as a late-cycle warning and shift probability mass toward bear, even if revenue_growth_yoy sits well above revenue_growth_mean_5y. A flat curve is not evidence that the warning is absent.

When the mean-reverted growth estimate (revenue_growth_mean_5y, adjusted by revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy) falls within one revenue_growth_std_5y of a bucket cutoff, do not put more than about 0.35 on the bucket on that side of the cutoff, and spread the rest across adjacent buckets (dalio.01, dalio.05). A wide std that leaves the central estimate close to a cutoff means the bucket call is close to a coin flip among neighbors.

When revenue_growth_yoy exceeds revenue_growth_mean_5y by more than one revenue_growth_std_5y, treat mean reversion toward the 5-year mean as the default and do not let an implied macro tailwind (revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy) move the bucket above that default unless a second macro input confirms it.

When revenue_macro_beta is large and the macro snapshot (gdp_growth_yoy, unemployment_rate, credit_spread_baa, yield_curve_10y_2y) is benign, apply the signed beta to the macro direction to shift the bucket upward or downward rather than treating the sign as neutral, and let recent revenue_growth_yoy above revenue_growth_mean_5y count as a tailwind.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits within one revenue_growth_std_5y of revenue_growth_mean_5y and revenue_macro_beta is high while the macro snapshot is benign (gdp_growth_yoy positive, yield_curve_10y_2y not inverted, credit_spread_baa low), do not default to the mean-reversion bucket. Let beta times the macro tailwind set the direction, and move the probability toward the bucket that the current growth rate supports.

When revenue_macro_beta has an unusual sign or magnitude, do not convert it into a growth drag by multiplying it by a macro snapshot such as gdp_growth_yoy unless a confirming signal is present (yield_curve_10y_2y < 0 or credit_spread_baa rising). Without that confirmation, anchor the central estimate on revenue_growth_mean_5y and treat the beta-implied drag as weak evidence.

When revenue_growth_yoy is only slightly above a bucket threshold and revenue_growth_mean_5y is missing, do not treat yoy persistence as the forecast; default to the bucket that contains the 5y mean (here base, 0-10%) and cap the upper-bucket probability, since mean reversion is the default. Missing distribution inputs such as revenue_growth_std_5y should widen the spread toward the middle bucket, not leave the call on the recent reading.

When revenue_macro_beta is well above 1 and gdp_growth_yoy is positive with yield_curve_10y_2y non-negative, treat the macro regime as amplifying growth and weight the bull bucket up, even if revenue_growth_yoy sits far above revenue_growth_mean_5y. Mean reversion should only cap the bull probability when the macro snapshot is weak or the curve is inverted.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is near flat (close to 0) and revenue_macro_beta is negative, treat the macro path as a downside regime and shift probability toward bear rather than reading the non-inverted curve as reassurance. Do not discount a metric like credit_spread_baa just because it lacks a trend.

When the central estimate sits within one revenue_growth_std_5y of a bucket threshold and yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero, cap the probability for that bucket near 0.5 and treat a flattening curve as a partial recession warning under dalio.03, not as no warning. Check the sign of each mean-reversion pull (revenue_growth_mean_5y versus revenue_growth_yoy) before using it to adjust the estimate.

When revenue_macro_beta is strongly negative (below -2) and yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero, treat the macro regime as a live downside risk and do not dismiss it because gdp_growth_yoy or unemployment_rate look stable, since those lag. Under those conditions, do not use revenue_growth_mean_5y as the central case when revenue_growth_yoy is far above it.

When revenue_macro_beta is above 1 and yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero (flattening toward inversion), treat the macro tilt as a downside risk and shift probability mass toward the bear band, even if revenue_growth_yoy sits in base. Do not read a barely positive yield curve as the absence of a slowdown signal.

When gdp_growth_yoy is strong (above about 2%), unemployment_rate is low, and yield_curve_10y_2y is positive, the macro regime is expansionary, so do not let revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy alone push the bucket toward bear. Anchor on revenue_growth_yoy and treat a negative revenue_growth_mean_5y as a weak pull, leaving base as the default bucket.

When revenue_growth_mean_5y sits within one revenue_growth_std_5y of a bucket threshold, cap the probability of the upper bucket well below 0.5 and move mass to the adjacent bucket, especially when revenue_macro_beta is above 2 and gdp_growth_yoy is weak. The analyst's own reasoning already said base was nearly as likely as bull, yet still assigned 0.5 to bull.

When revenue_growth_yoy is positive and above revenue_growth_mean_5y, do not let the negative 5-year mean set the bucket; treat a revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy drag as a bear tilt only if yield_curve_10y_2y is below zero or credit_spread_baa is rising.

When revenue_macro_beta is strongly negative (for example below -5) and yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero, do not dismiss the beta because no outright recession signal is visible. Multiply it by the macro snapshot and shift probability toward bear, and cap the bull probability when revenue_growth_yoy sits far above revenue_growth_mean_5y.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits well above revenue_growth_mean_5y (more than one revenue_growth_std_5y), do not let a linear revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy headwind override recent momentum toward bear unless yield_curve_10y_2y is negative or credit_spread_baa is clearly rising. A large beta-implied drag with no confirming credit or curve signal should lower the bear probability, not raise it.

When revenue_growth_yoy exceeds revenue_growth_mean_5y by more than one revenue_growth_std_5y, and revenue_macro_beta is high while yield_curve_10y_2y is positive and unemployment_rate is low, do not default to mean reversion toward the base band. Treat revenue_macro_beta as amplifying upside in an expansion as well as downside, and give the bull bucket real weight.

When revenue_macro_beta is strongly negative (about -5 or lower) and yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero, weight the bear tail heavily and do not assign more than about 0.5 to base, even when revenue_growth_yoy sits at revenue_growth_mean_5y. Flagging a large macro beta and then dismissing it is not a valid reason to keep the base case.

When revenue_macro_beta is materially negative (around -0.5 or lower), treat the macro drag as a directional shift toward the bear band, and do not dismiss it because gdp_growth_yoy and unemployment_rate show no recession. Move the bear probability up in proportion to the beta before settling on base, and cap the probability on the base band when revenue_growth_std_5y is wide.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero (flat, not clearly positive) or credit_spread_baa is elevated and its trend is unknown, do not treat them as neutral. Move probability toward the bear bucket and lower confidence in base, especially when revenue_macro_beta is above 1 or revenue_growth_yoy is already below revenue_growth_mean_5y.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits far above a bucket threshold but revenue_growth_mean_5y or revenue_growth_std_5y is missing, do not treat the yoy print as a directional lead: keep the bucket probability near the uninformed baseline, because without the 5y mean and std the reading cannot be placed in its distribution (dalio.05).

When revenue_growth_yoy sits above revenue_growth_mean_5y, the reversion anchor is revenue_growth_mean_5y itself: if that mean is negative, the central estimate must sit below 0% and the bear bucket must get the largest probability unless revenue_macro_beta times the macro snapshot offers a clear offset. Do not assign base the majority when the mean-reversion target falls in the bear bucket.

When revenue_growth_mean_5y sits within about 0.01 of a bucket threshold and revenue_growth_std_5y is above roughly 0.04, cap the probability of the nearest bucket near 0.5 and spread the rest across adjacent buckets, using revenue_macro_beta to widen the spread when yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero. Do not let a point estimate just above a threshold support a confident call.

When revenue_macro_beta is negative and yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero (within about 0.25 pp of inversion), treat the macro drag (revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy) as a regime signal that can override the revenue_growth_mean_5y anchor, and cut the bull probability rather than dismissing the drag as minor. A flat curve is a warning under dalio.03, not a neutral reading.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits in a higher bucket than revenue_growth_mean_5y, anchor the forecast on the 5-year mean as the default and move toward the yoy print only in proportion to how low revenue_growth_std_5y is. A negative revenue_growth_mean_5y should pull the bucket toward bear, not be offset by a macro-beta upside argument.

When revenue_growth_yoy already sits in the base band and revenue_macro_beta is negative with yield_curve_10y_2y near zero, do not let revenue_growth_mean_5y alone move the bucket to bull; anchor on the recent run-rate, and cut bull probability further when revenue_growth_std_5y is wide.

When revenue_macro_beta is high (above about 5) and yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero (below about 0.005), treat the yield curve as a live recession warning and move probability mass from base toward bear, rather than dismissing it because the curve is still technically positive. Cap base confidence when revenue_growth_std_5y is also wide.

When revenue_growth_yoy is positive but revenue_growth_mean_5y is negative, treat the one-year reading as weak evidence and default toward the 5y mean; with a high revenue_macro_beta and a yield_curve_10y_2y near zero, shift probability toward the bear bucket rather than base.

When gdp_growth_yoy is positive, unemployment_rate is low, and credit_spread_baa is at a non-stressed level, do not let a large revenue_macro_beta alone push the call to bear. Check whether the benign macro snapshot offsets the implied drag, and widen the base band before assigning high bear probability.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is within about 0.25 points of zero, or revenue_macro_beta is below -1.0, treat the macro backdrop as a downside risk: cap any bull probability at 0.5 unless credit_spread_baa is falling, and do not dismiss a near-flat curve as 'no inversion.'

When revenue_growth_std_5y is wide (around 0.05 or more) and yield_curve_10y_2y and gdp_growth_yoy are non-negative, do not put more than about 0.4 on a single bucket even if revenue_growth_yoy and revenue_growth_mean_5y both point to it; spread probability into the adjacent bucket, since mean reversion pulls growth toward the middle of the distribution.

When revenue_macro_beta is well above 1 and gdp_growth_yoy is running above its typical level, shift the central revenue estimate in the direction of beta times the macro gap rather than only widening the distribution, and do not anchor on revenue_growth_mean_5y alone.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is within about 0.5 percentage points of zero, treat it as a flattening warning under dalio.03 and move probability mass toward the bear bucket, rather than dismissing it because it is not strictly negative. Also, when revenue_growth_mean_5y and revenue_growth_std_5y are both missing, do not put more than about 0.4 on any single bucket.

When revenue_growth_std_5y is at least as wide as a bucket (about 0.10), cap any single-bucket probability near 0.40 and spread the remainder across the adjacent buckets, because mean reversion toward revenue_growth_mean_5y sets the center of the distribution but not the confidence in one band.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero (roughly below 0.005) and revenue_growth_yoy is negative, treat the flat curve as a bear warning under dalio.03 rather than as absence of a recession signal, and do not let revenue_growth_mean_5y anchor the call toward base.

When revenue_macro_beta is strongly negative (below -2) and yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero, treat the macro backdrop as a downside regime and move probability mass from base toward bear rather than calling the macro evidence mixed. Mean reversion to revenue_growth_mean_5y should not override a large negative revenue_macro_beta.

When revenue_macro_beta is strongly negative but gdp_growth_yoy is positive and unemployment_rate is low, do not treat the beta-times-GDP product as a contraction forecast; move to bear only when yield_curve_10y_2y is below zero or credit_spread_baa is rising, and otherwise anchor on revenue_growth_yoy with mean reversion toward revenue_growth_mean_5y.

When the blended growth estimate (recent revenue_growth_yoy, revenue_growth_mean_5y, and the macro tilt) falls within one revenue_growth_std_5y of a bucket boundary, cap the modal bucket's probability near 0.4 and split the remaining mass across the adjacent buckets instead of assigning 0.5 to the modal bucket.

When revenue_growth_std_5y is large relative to the gap between revenue_growth_yoy and a bucket boundary, cap the modal bucket's probability well below 0.7 and treat a large revenue_macro_beta as real macro sensitivity, not a units error that can be dismissed. Confidence should shrink as the std of growth rises (dalio.05).

When revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy is strongly negative (about -0.2 here), treat it as a primary bear signal that moves the bucket probabilities, not a minor tilt, and do not discount it because the unit scale is uncertain, especially when yield_curve_10y_2y is only barely positive and credit_spread_baa has not been checked for a rising trend.

When revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy implies a tailwind larger than the gap between revenue_growth_yoy and the bull threshold, or when revenue_growth_mean_5y sits well above revenue_growth_yoy, do not set those metrics aside as unverified or as weak anchors because revenue_growth_std_5y is wide; use them to move the center of the distribution toward the bucket they point to, and only then widen it.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits above revenue_growth_mean_5y, shrink toward the 5y mean by default, and do not let the revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy product or a near-zero yield_curve_10y_2y be read as upside support. Treat a flat yield curve as a bear-leaning warning and move probability toward bear when the spread is near zero.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one revenue_growth_std_5y above revenue_growth_mean_5y, shrink the forecast back toward revenue_growth_mean_5y before choosing a bucket, and do not make bull the modal bucket if revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy is materially negative. Mean reversion is the default (dalio.04), and a large negative macro term should move the mode toward base.

When revenue_growth_yoy exceeds revenue_growth_mean_5y by less than one revenue_growth_std_5y, treat the 5-year mean as the central case and the recent reading as a deviation that tends to revert, so a bull call needs the yoy reading to clear the bull threshold on its own. A yield_curve_10y_2y near zero should be read as a bear-leaning warning, not as a neutral non-negative reading, and should cap bull probability.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero (flat, not clearly positive) and revenue_growth_std_5y is above 0.15, do not treat the absence of an inverted curve as a clean all-clear. Instead, weight the bear bucket by revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy as a downside channel, and keep the base probability below 0.5 (dalio.03, dalio.02).

When yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero (here 0.0025) and not clearly positive, treat it as a flattening warning under dalio.03 and shift probability toward the bear bucket, rather than reading it as absence of bear signal. Do not let a large revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy product override that warning.

When revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy implies a headwind and revenue_growth_yoy is already negative, treat that as a regime shift that moves the center toward bear, even if yield_curve_10y_2y is slightly positive. Do not let a near-zero yield_curve_10y_2y veto the headwind, and do not default to reversion toward revenue_growth_mean_5y.

When revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy is below -0.1 and revenue_growth_yoy sits near 0%, treat the macro drag as the dominant signal and give bear at least as much probability as base, since a near-zero yield_curve_10y_2y is not evidence against bear. Do not dismiss a large macro-beta effect as unit uncertainty when it is the only metric pointing at the bucket that later occurred.

When revenue_growth_std_5y is large relative to the distance from revenue_growth_mean_5y to a bucket boundary, compute that boundary's tail mass from the normal approximation and do not cap the neighbouring bucket below it, even when macro inputs look benign. Shrink the modal probability as the std rises (dalio.05).

When yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero (below 0.01) and revenue_growth_yoy sits above revenue_growth_mean_5y, treat the late-cycle flattening as a regime warning: cap the bull probability and shift weight toward base and bear, since persistence of the recent reading is not the default. Mean reversion toward revenue_growth_mean_5y governs unless the curve is clearly positive and widening spreads are absent.

When revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy implies a tailwind of about 10% or more and yield_curve_10y_2y is not inverted (at or above 0), treat that macro tailwind as primary evidence and shift probability toward bull. A flat but non-negative yield curve is not a warning under dalio.03, so it should not be used to discount the macro signal.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is near or below zero and revenue_growth_yoy is already falling below revenue_growth_mean_5y with a negative revenue_macro_beta drag, treat the macro regime as turning down and do not default to mean reversion toward the 5y mean (dalio.04); shift weight into the bear bucket instead of only capping bull.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is at or near zero, treat it as a bear-leaning growth warning, and when the mean-reverted central estimate sits below 0%, give bear the largest probability, not base, rather than letting the curve only cap the bull case. This applies dalio.03 and dalio.04 to the bucket split.

When revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy implies a drag that is large relative to revenue_growth_yoy, do not discard it as a unit error without verifying the input; treat it as a live warning and cap the bull probability until it is resolved. Also cap bull when revenue_growth_std_5y is large relative to the bull threshold (dalio.05).

When yield_curve_10y_2y is at or above 0, do not treat it as a growth warning, since dalio.03 only fires on an inverted curve. When a revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy drag is the main reason for a bear call, shrink that drag toward zero unless revenue_growth_yoy is also falling below revenue_growth_mean_5y.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero (say below 0.01), treat it as an active growth warning under dalio.03: do not apply the revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy tailwind, and shift probability toward bear when revenue_growth_yoy is already above revenue_growth_mean_5y.

When revenue_growth_std_5y is larger than the gap between the mean-reverted estimate and an adjacent bucket cutoff, cap the leading bucket's probability near 0.4 and give the adjacent bucket on the side of a negative revenue_growth_yoy at least 0.3, since a flat yield_curve_10y_2y does not offset the downside. (dalio.05, dalio.01)

When revenue_growth_yoy is negative and the macro product revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy points positive, do not let the macro product lift the central estimate above the trailing reading; anchor on revenue_growth_yoy with mean reversion toward revenue_growth_mean_5y, and cap bucket probability when revenue_growth_std_5y is wide.

When revenue_growth_std_5y is at least about one-third of revenue_growth_mean_5y, do not treat a bucket boundary within about 1.5 std of the mean as a tail. Keep the modal bucket below about 0.5 and assign real mass to the adjacent bucket, per dalio.05 and dalio.01.

When revenue_growth_std_5y is above roughly 0.05, cap any single revenue bucket probability near 0.45 and compute bear mass from a distribution centered on revenue_growth_mean_5y, not revenue_growth_yoy. A near-zero yield_curve_10y_2y should also shift mass toward bear rather than only capping bull.

When revenue_macro_beta is well above 1 and yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero, do not read revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy as a net tailwind; a flattening curve signals a regime where high beta amplifies downside, so shift probability mass toward the bear bucket. This applies dalio.02 and dalio.03.

When revenue_growth_std_5y is large relative to the gap between revenue_growth_mean_5y and the 0% bear cutoff, derive bucket probabilities from the normal distribution those two metrics imply and cap the modal bucket near 0.4, rather than letting a macro tailwind from revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy push it higher.

When revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy implies a tailwind near or above the 10% bull cutoff and gdp_growth_yoy is positive, do not discount that tailwind because credit_spread_baa lacks a trend reading. Treat the missing credit confirmation as a reason to widen the distribution, and shift probability toward bull rather than keeping base as the modal outcome.

When revenue_macro_beta is very large (for example above 5) and yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero, do not discount the beta as a scale artifact. Multiply it by the macro snapshot to get an implied revenue shift, and let that shift tilt the bucket toward bear before relying on strong gdp_growth_yoy.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero (flat, roughly 0 or below), treat it as a late-cycle regime warning that overrides persistence from revenue_growth_yoy and does not justify a bull tilt. Discount any tailwind from revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy until the curve steepens, and shift probability toward base and bear.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits below revenue_growth_mean_5y, treat mean reversion toward the 5y mean as the default even if revenue_growth_std_5y is wide, and do not let a revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy product drive a bear call unless yield_curve_10y_2y is negative or credit_spread_baa is rising. A near-zero or positive yield_curve_10y_2y is not an inversion warning.

When revenue_growth_mean_5y is negative and revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one revenue_growth_std_5y above it, the modal bucket should be the one the 5y mean pulls toward (bear), not the bucket the recent reading suggests, because mean reversion is the default. Weaken that shift only when a confirming trend in credit_spread_baa or yield_curve_10y_2y is present.

When revenue_growth_std_5y is wide enough that one std spans roughly half of a bucket's width, cap the leading bucket's probability well below 0.5 and keep the bear tail open, even when revenue_growth_yoy sits inside the base band. Do not net revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy into a single point estimate that narrows the distribution.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is still positive, do not treat it as a growth warning or trim the bull share; apply dalio.03 only when yield_curve_10y_2y < 0 and credit_spread_baa is rising. Otherwise let the revenue_growth_mean_5y and revenue_growth_std_5y distribution set the bucket probabilities.

When revenue_macro_beta is high (above about 1.5) and yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero (below about 0.01), classify the macro regime as late-cycle rather than expansionary, and shift probability mass from base toward bear, with credit_spread_baa as the confirming check. Do not let solid current gdp_growth_yoy or unemployment_rate offset a flattening curve on a high-beta business.

When revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy implies a drag larger than revenue_growth_std_5y, treat it as a linear extrapolation and anchor to revenue_growth_mean_5y, keeping the bear probability near the base rate unless yield_curve_10y_2y is negative and credit_spread_baa is confirmed rising.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero (flat) and revenue_macro_beta is large, do not discount the beta as implausible. Treat the combination as a regime warning that moves mass toward base and bear, and cut the bull probability when revenue_growth_yoy is below revenue_growth_mean_5y.

When revenue_growth_yoy is negative and more than one revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y, do not assume mean reversion to the base band; treat the negative yoy sign as the leading signal and give bear at least equal weight to base, with confidence capped by revenue_growth_std_5y.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero or credit_spread_baa is wide, do not discount them for lacking a trend reading; treat them as evidence of late-cycle weakness and move probability mass toward bear, especially when revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy is used to justify a tailwind.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than 2 revenue_growth_std_5y away from revenue_growth_mean_5y, do not treat mean reversion as settling the bucket; cap the modal bucket probability near 0.4 and keep the opposite-side tail bucket (here bull) at a material share, since a gap of about 1.4 std to the bull threshold is still reachable.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero (flat) and revenue_macro_beta is above 1, read the beta as a downside amplifier of any slowdown, not as a tailwind from revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy, and shift probability toward bear before relying on mean reversion toward revenue_growth_mean_5y.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is positive, do not treat a near-zero reading as a recession warning under dalio.03; that warning requires an inverted curve (below 0). When revenue_growth_yoy sits above revenue_growth_mean_5y, let that recent print counter a macro-beta drag, instead of leaning bear on the drag alone.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y, do not treat mean reversion toward the 5y mean as the default upward pull; treat the deceleration as the leading signal, and when yield_curve_10y_2y is within a few basis points of zero, count it as a warning and raise bear probability.

When revenue_macro_beta is high (above 0.5) and unemployment_rate is elevated while gdp_growth_yoy is near zero, treat the setup as a possible cyclical rebound and give the bull bucket a materially larger share, instead of dismissing the slack as a bear-only signal or calling the GDP drag negligible. Mean reversion toward revenue_growth_mean_5y should not be the default when the macro regime is shifting.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is still positive, do not shift probability toward bear on curve grounds; apply the dalio.03 bear tilt only when yield_curve_10y_2y < 0. When revenue_macro_beta is high (above 1), scale the macro move by revenue_macro_beta before treating it as a small drag.

When unemployment_rate is elevated and revenue_growth_yoy sits within one revenue_growth_std_5y of the 0% bear cutoff, do not let mean reversion toward revenue_growth_mean_5y carry the base band; shift probability toward bear and cap base confidence well below 0.45.

When revenue_growth_yoy falls more than one revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y, anchor the bucket on revenue_growth_mean_5y rather than the recent print, and do not treat a near-zero yield_curve_10y_2y as a bear signal unless credit_spread_baa is also rising. Shift toward bear only when both gdp_growth_yoy and revenue_macro_beta times that GDP reading confirm weakness.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is non-negative, do not treat it as the inversion warning in dalio.03, and do not use it to cap the bull bucket; reserve that warning for yield_curve_10y_2y < 0. When revenue_growth_yoy sits well above revenue_growth_mean_5y and revenue_macro_beta is high, keep bull mass in the distribution even if gdp_growth_yoy is weak.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than 2 std above revenue_growth_mean_5y and the macro drag (revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy) is near zero, weight the recent growth run-rate above mean reversion and do not let a negative revenue_macro_beta or a flat yield_curve_10y_2y alone move probability toward bear or away from bull.

When revenue_growth_yoy is positive and sits above revenue_growth_mean_5y by more than half of revenue_growth_std_5y, do not anchor the bucket on the negative 5y mean alone; blend recent growth with the mean and keep bear as the top bucket only if that blended central estimate is below 0%. A small revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy drag should not override a positive revenue_growth_yoy.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is still non-negative, do not treat a value near zero as a recession warning; shift probability toward bear only when yield_curve_10y_2y < 0 (dalio.03). Otherwise let revenue_growth_yoy's reversion toward revenue_growth_mean_5y set the center, which here favors base.

When gdp_growth_yoy is near zero and unemployment_rate is high (above about 0.10) alongside a flat yield_curve_10y_2y, treat the macro regime as contractionary and let it set the center of the distribution before any revenue_growth_mean_5y anchor. Do not put bull above 0.3 unless revenue_growth_yoy is above 0.10 and the macro snapshot does not contradict it.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is still positive, do not treat it as the dalio.03 inversion warning; apply that warning only when the curve is below 0. When revenue_growth_std_5y is wide, anchor the mean-reversion target on revenue_growth_mean_5y and keep bull and bear probabilities uncapped rather than fixing the modal bucket at base.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than 2 revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y, treat the reading as a likely transitory shock rather than a trend, and do not let it alone set a bear probability above about 0.5 unless revenue_growth_mean_5y is itself in bear and the macro drag is confirmed by a second independent metric. Recent extreme readings can revert past the 5y mean, so keep the bull and base buckets materially weighted.

When revenue_growth_std_5y is wide (above about 0.25), cap the modal bucket's probability near 0.5 and keep at least 0.2 on the bucket opposite the sign of revenue_growth_yoy, since a large deviation from revenue_growth_mean_5y can still mean-revert upward after a deep trough. The reasoning should not contradict itself by stating confidence must stay below 0.7 and then assigning 0.68.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than two revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y, treat the gap as a mean-reversion setup under dalio.04 and do not put bear above base unless yield_curve_10y_2y is below zero and credit_spread_baa is rising; a slightly positive yield_curve_10y_2y is not a recession signal.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than 2 revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y, cap the probability on the extreme bucket well below 0.6 and widen the base band, because the reading is more likely to revert than persist. Do not raise confidence from a macro multiplier like revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy unless a trend-confirming signal such as a rising credit_spread_baa is actually present.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y, treat the gap as a likely reversion toward the mean and do not let that single reading plus a macro drag from revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy set a bear bucket unless a trend in credit_spread_baa or yield_curve_10y_2y confirms the downturn.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is above zero, dalio.03 gives no weakness warning, so a flat curve must not be counted as a growth headwind. When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than 3 revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y, treat it as a possible one-off and let revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy drive a bear call only if credit_spread_baa is also rising.

When revenue_growth_yoy is negative but revenue_growth_mean_5y is positive, anchor the central estimate on the 5y mean (dalio.04 mean reversion) and let a wide revenue_growth_std_5y spread the probability mass rather than discounting the mean. Do not let revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy alone set a bear call.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than 2 std below revenue_growth_mean_5y, treat the extreme print as a possible transient shock rather than a trend: centre the forecast on revenue_growth_mean_5y with revenue_growth_std_5y as the spread, and do not let the raw yoy value drive the bear probability above what that distribution supports.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than two revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y, anchor the forecast on mean reversion to that mean and move the bear probability on macro inputs only if yield_curve_10y_2y is below 0 or credit_spread_baa is rising, not on a positive revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy product or a near-flat yield curve.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y, treat the gap as likely to revert toward revenue_growth_mean_5y and do not put bear above base unless gdp_growth_yoy and yield_curve_10y_2y both confirm a downturn. A single weak print with a flat curve is not enough to override the mean-reversion default.

When revenue_growth_mean_5y or revenue_growth_std_5y is missing, cap the probability on any single bucket well below 0.8 and do not treat an extreme revenue_growth_yoy as persistent; default to reversion toward the typical range, as dalio.04 says.

When the central estimate (the revenue_growth_mean_5y anchor, plus any revenue_macro_beta times macro adjustment) lies within one revenue_growth_std_5y of a bucket boundary, cap that bucket's probability near 0.5 and put the remaining mass on the adjacent bucket. Do not set bear above 0.5 when the central estimate is only about 0.5 percentage points below the 0% cutoff.

When revenue_growth_std_5y is wide (above about 0.2), cap the probability of any single revenue bucket at roughly 0.4 and treat a large revenue_growth_yoy deviation from revenue_growth_mean_5y as a reason to widen the distribution, not to concentrate it on the bear bucket. A macro drag from revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy should only raise bear confidence when it agrees with the yoy reading.

When credit_spread_baa is flat or not widening and yield_curve_10y_2y is near or above zero, do not treat the product of revenue_macro_beta and a negative gdp_growth_yoy as a bear tilt; require a rising credit_spread_baa, per dalio.03, before applying a macro drag to the bucket probabilities.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits below revenue_growth_mean_5y, mean reversion (dalio.04) points the central estimate up toward the 5y mean, not further down; do not extrapolate the recent decline, and check the sign of the reversion before applying any macro drag from revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y, treat the gap as a reversion setup and spread probability into the bull tail rather than anchoring on the reverted mean. Do not let a small negative gdp_growth_yoy multiplied by a large revenue_macro_beta set the bucket direction on its own.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y, read the gap as mean reversion pointing up toward the 5y mean, not as bear evidence. Let a revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy drag push the call toward bear only when yield_curve_10y_2y is below zero and credit_spread_baa is rising.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y, treat the drop as a possible cyclical trough rather than persistent momentum, and do not use the gap to rule out base. Keep the bucket probabilities close to the distribution implied by revenue_growth_mean_5y and revenue_growth_std_5y, and let a weak yoy reading move the estimate only partway.

When yield_curve_10y_2y is non-inverted (>= 0) and credit_spread_baa has no rising trend, do not treat a small revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy drag as enough to move the central estimate across 0%; when the central estimate is within about 0.5 revenue_growth_std_5y of the 0% boundary, keep base as the modal bucket rather than bear (dalio.02, dalio.03, dalio.05).

When revenue_growth_yoy sits well below revenue_growth_mean_5y, mean reversion (dalio.04) implies growth recovers toward the mean, so the gap's direction sets the expected move and the mean's sign should not be read as the bucket. Raise base and bull weight in that case, and check whether the depressed trailing base makes the next four quarters' comparison easier before leaning bear.

When revenue_growth_yoy falls more than about 1.5 revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y while gdp_growth_yoy is only mildly negative and yield_curve_10y_2y stays positive, treat the extreme print as a possible trough or base effect rather than a bear trend, and do not let it alone set the bear probability above about 0.4.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits below revenue_growth_mean_5y, mean reversion points up toward the mean, so the reversion term must add probability to the base and bull buckets, not to bear. Sign the reversion direction from the gap between revenue_growth_yoy and revenue_growth_mean_5y before weighting any bucket.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits less than one revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y and yield_curve_10y_2y is positive, do not treat the trailing print as bear-confirming; weight mean reversion toward revenue_growth_mean_5y and spread probability across base and bull, since a single weak yoy reading in a wide-std series is not strong evidence of persistence.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y, treat the gap as a trough that mean-reverts upward toward the 5y mean, not as momentum toward more decline. Mean reversion must be signed toward revenue_growth_mean_5y, and a deep negative reading should not by itself justify a bear call.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than 2 revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y, the reading is an outlier, so mean reversion (dalio.04) points toward the mean, which is upward for a deeply negative print. Do not read it as a bear signal, and treat the macro term (revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy) as too unreliable to dominate when revenue_macro_beta is extreme.

When revenue_growth_std_5y is above 0.2 and revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one std below revenue_growth_mean_5y, cap any single bucket probability well below 0.45 and move meaningful mass to bull, since a sharp drop in a high-variance series often reverts past its mean rather than settling at it.

When revenue_growth_std_5y is above roughly 0.08 and the 5y mean sits inside one bucket, cap that bucket's probability near 0.35 and assign explicit mass to the tail bucket more than one std from the mean, instead of letting mean reversion alone set the answer. Here the tail was bull, which the analyst never weighed.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits well below revenue_growth_mean_5y, mean reversion (dalio.04) points upward toward the mean, so it supports base or bull rather than bear, and a yield_curve_10y_2y reading that is still positive should not be counted as a recession warning unless it is below zero (dalio.03).

When gdp_growth_yoy is negative but yield_curve_10y_2y is positive and credit_spread_baa shows no widening, do not let revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy set the bear tilt. Anchor the central estimate on revenue_growth_mean_5y and keep the macro shift small relative to revenue_growth_std_5y, so bucket odds near the 0% cutoff stay close to even.

When abs(revenue_growth_mean_5y) is smaller than revenue_growth_std_5y and yield_curve_10y_2y is positive with no confirmed credit_spread_baa trend, cap the probability of the bucket that the mean sits in at about one-third and spread the remainder across the neighbouring buckets.

When revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy is positive, do not dismiss it just because yield_curve_10y_2y is non-negative; treat the positive product as a counter-signal and pull any bear probability toward 0.5 unless the product turns negative, since the macro regime can outweigh a large negative revenue_growth_yoy versus revenue_growth_mean_5y gap.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y, read the gap as a mean-reversion pull toward the 5y mean, not as a continuation signal, and do not put bear above base or bull unless yield_curve_10y_2y is negative or credit_spread_baa is rising. Check that the revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy tailwind is weighed against the trailing decline rather than dismissed.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y and revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy is positive, treat the trailing drop as a possible trough, not a persistent signal, and do not let bear take the modal bucket on the trailing reading alone. Give bull and base real weight, since a high-beta business with a positive macro product tends to rebound from a deep trough.

When revenue_growth_yoy exceeds revenue_growth_mean_5y by more than half a revenue_growth_std_5y and revenue_macro_beta is above 1 with yield_curve_10y_2y positive, weight persistence of recent growth over mean reversion and raise the bull bucket above the base bucket instead of anchoring the central estimate near the 5y mean.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits above the bull threshold and no macro trigger is present (yield_curve_10y_2y positive, credit_spread_baa not rising, gdp_growth_yoy not contracting), treat yoy persistence as the primary signal and only shift toward revenue_growth_mean_5y when a macro or credit reading confirms a downturn. Do not let the mean alone pull the bucket below the threshold.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one revenue_growth_std_5y below revenue_growth_mean_5y, treat the drop as a candidate for mean reversion under dalio.04 rather than a leading bear signal, and do not read a positive yield_curve_10y_2y as a flattening warning, since dalio.03 requires an inverted curve (below 0).

When yield_curve_10y_2y is positive, do not apply the dalio.03 flattening warning or shift mass toward bear; apply that warning only when yield_curve_10y_2y is below zero. When revenue_growth_yoy sits well above revenue_growth_mean_5y, weigh its persistence against mean reversion instead of treating the 5y mean as the default anchor.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one revenue_growth_std_5y above revenue_growth_mean_5y and gdp_growth_yoy is still positive, treat recent growth as the center of the distribution and do not let the mean-reversion pull toward bear dominate. Mean reversion should be a partial drag, not the default that overrides a persistent upswing.

When revenue_growth_yoy is within one revenue_growth_std_5y of 0% and revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy is positive, set the bucket from the macro-adjusted center rather than from revenue_growth_mean_5y alone, because the 5y mean can lean the label toward bear even when the center sits in base. Label the most likely bucket from that center, then size the probability from the spread.

When gdp_growth_yoy is weak (below about 0.01) and yield_curve_10y_2y is near flat (below about 0.02), treat the macro regime as a slowdown and move probability toward bear. Do not treat a near-zero product of revenue_macro_beta and gdp_growth_yoy as proof that macro is neutral, because a small product can come from a small GDP level rather than from a benign environment.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one revenue_growth_std_5y above revenue_growth_mean_5y, treat the print as a likely reversion toward the 5y mean and do not let it, or a macro beta times gdp_growth_yoy tailwind, carry the bull call; anchor the bucket distribution on revenue_growth_mean_5y and cap the bull probability well below 0.45 unless the macro tailwind is confirmed independently of trailing growth.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than 2 times revenue_growth_std_5y above revenue_growth_mean_5y, treat the reading as likely transitory per dalio.04 and anchor the distribution on revenue_growth_mean_5y, keeping bull probability below base unless a macro input such as revenue_macro_beta times the macro snapshot independently supports the higher bucket.

When credit_spread_baa is available, treat its level as a weakening-growth signal even without a trend reading, and when it combines with a near-flat yield_curve_10y_2y and negative revenue_macro_beta, cap bull probability and move mass into base. Do not set a metric aside as unconfirmed just because its trend is missing.

When revenue_growth_std_5y is above about 0.05 and the blended central estimate sits within one std of a bucket edge (here the 0% bear cutoff), cap the modal bucket near 0.35-0.40 and give the adjacent bucket at least 0.25, even if revenue_growth_yoy falls in the base band. A negative revenue_macro_beta should be treated as a real bear tilt, not a small drag to net away.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than 1.5 revenue_growth_std_5y above revenue_growth_mean_5y, make base the modal bucket and do not let the macro tailwind from revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy override the mean-reversion pull (dalio.04) toward base; bull can only be modal if the recent growth is supported by more than the macro product.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than 2 revenue_growth_std_5y above revenue_growth_mean_5y, treat the spike as a probable one-off and anchor the bucket distribution to revenue_growth_mean_5y, not to revenue_growth_yoy or a revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy tailwind. Only lift bull probability when the macro snapshot and the trend confirm the reading.

When gdp_growth_yoy is above 10% and revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy implies a tailwind of 5 points or more, the macro expansion regime should override the default pull of revenue_growth_mean_5y, and the bull bucket should carry the largest probability mass. Mean reversion should only be allowed to dominate when the macro tailwind is small or the credit and curve signals are weakening.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one revenue_growth_std_5y above revenue_growth_mean_5y, do not center the forecast on the recent run-rate. Revert toward revenue_growth_mean_5y first, and assign bull only if the revenue_macro_beta tailwind still clears the bull cutoff after that reversion, with probability capped by the width of revenue_growth_std_5y.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than 2 revenue_growth_std_5y above revenue_growth_mean_5y, treat the print as a likely transient spike and anchor the bucket distribution on revenue_growth_mean_5y, rather than extrapolating it. Do not credit revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy as a macro tailwind when the beta is implausibly large (above about 2), and cap bull probability unless the spike persists in later periods.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits more than 2 revenue_growth_std_5y above revenue_growth_mean_5y, do not let a single-year gdp_growth_yoy tailwind through revenue_macro_beta lift the bull probability above the base mass; mean reversion (dalio.04) governs, so cap bull near 0.3 unless revenue_growth_mean_5y has also risen.

When the macro-implied growth (revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy) lands below the bull cutoff, or yield_curve_10y_2y is near zero, treat those as a cap on the bull case and move probability mass to base, even if revenue_growth_yoy is above 10%. A macro-implied figure in the base band should not be cited as support for bull.

When revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy implies a tailwind of about 3 points or more and credit_spread_baa is low, treat the macro regime as the primary driver and shift probability toward the bull bucket instead of letting revenue_growth_mean_5y anchor the center. Mean reversion should be the default only when the macro tailwind is small.

When revenue_growth_yoy is negative and revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy is also negative, do not let revenue_growth_mean_5y set the modal bucket by default; treat bear as at least co-modal with base and reserve mean reversion for cases where recent growth is positive.

When revenue_growth_yoy sits well above revenue_growth_mean_5y, shrink the forecast toward revenue_growth_mean_5y and make the modal bucket the one containing that mean unless a confirmed macro signal (inverted yield_curve_10y_2y or rising credit_spread_baa) supports a different bucket. Momentum and a positive macro tailwind alone should not override mean reversion when revenue_growth_std_5y is wide.

When revenue_growth_yoy exceeds revenue_growth_mean_5y by more than one revenue_growth_std_5y, anchor the distribution on the 5y mean rather than the spike, and cap any bull probability at the share the mean-anchored distribution supports, with the rest going to base. Do not let a positive revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy tailwind lift bull above that cap.

When the central revenue estimate sits within one revenue_growth_std_5y of a bucket boundary, do not give the bucket above that boundary the modal probability; cap it near 0.33 and move the mass to the adjacent bucket, as dalio.05 requires for wide distributions.

When revenue_growth_yoy exceeds revenue_growth_mean_5y by roughly one revenue_growth_std_5y or more, treat the print as transient and anchor the modal bucket on revenue_growth_mean_5y. A revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy tailwind should shift probability mass within that anchored distribution, not promote the bucket above base.

When revenue_macro_beta is well above 1 and gdp_growth_yoy is positive with unemployment_rate low and yield_curve_10y_2y non-negative, treat the expansion as the regime and let the beta-times-GDP tailwind move the modal bucket toward bull. Use revenue_growth_mean_5y as the anchor only when credit_spread_baa is rising or yield_curve_10y_2y is inverted.

When revenue_macro_beta times gdp_growth_yoy puts the macro tailwind at or near the 10% bull cutoff and revenue_growth_yoy sits more than one revenue_growth_std_5y above revenue_growth_mean_5y, treat the regime as sustaining growth and weight bull above base instead of defaulting to mean reversion. A yield_curve_10y_2y that is near zero but not negative, with a non-stressed credit_spread_baa, does not cap bull under dalio.03.

When revenue_growth_std_5y is wide, compute each bucket's mass from a distribution centered on revenue_growth_mean_5y with that std, and make the modal bucket the one with the largest mass rather than the band containing the mean. Cap the reported probability at that computed mass, since a 0.12 std with a 0.025 mean puts roughly 0.42 in bear and only about 0.31 in base (dalio.01, dalio.05).
